title: How do you build a successful team? With Eduardo Salas, PhD

sentences.en: Before we get started today, I'd like to ask you to take a moment to fill out our listener survey.
sentences.zh: 在我们今天开始之前，我想请大家花点时间填写我们的听众调查问卷。

sentences.en: We want to know more about you, what you think of this podcast, and what you'd like to hear more from us.
sentences.zh: 我们想更多地了解你、你对这个播客的看法，以及你希望我们制作更多什么样的内容。

sentences.en: So if you could, please go to our show notes at Apple Podcasts, Spotify, or wherever you listen to Speaking of Psychology,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果可以的话，请前往 Apple Podcasts、Spotify 或你收听《心理学聊天室》的任何平台上的节目简介，

sentences.en: or go to our website at www.speakingofpsychology.org and look for the link to the listener survey.
sentences.zh: 或者访问我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology.org，寻找听众调查问卷的链接。

sentences.en: We'd really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们将不胜感激。

sentences.en: Now, on to the episode.
sentences.zh: 现在，进入本期节目。

sentences.en: Very few people do their jobs entirely on their own.
sentences.zh: 极少有人能完全靠自己完成工作。

sentences.en: For most of us, our work is enmeshed with other people's work, and doing our job well often means being part of a well-functioning team.
sentences.zh: 对我们大多数人而言，我们的工作与他人的工作盘根错节，而把工作做好通常意味着成为一个高效运转的团队的一部分。

sentences.en: The stakes of teamwork can be high, especially in workplaces where errors have dire consequences, such as emergency rooms or air traffic control towers.
sentences.zh: 团队合作的利害攸关，特别是在那些错误会带来严重后果的工作场所，比如急诊室或空中交通管制塔台。

sentences.en: In those settings, a breakdown in teamwork can be the difference between life and death.
sentences.zh: 在这些环境中，团队合作的崩溃可能意味着生与死的差别。

sentences.en: Over the past decades, psychologist research has helped organizations from hospitals to military units to airlines develop better functioning and more effective teaMs.
sentences.zh: 在过去的几十年里，心理学研究一直帮助从医院、军队到航空公司的各种组织开发出运转更良好、更有效的团队。

sentences.en: So what does good teamwork look like?
sentences.zh: 那么，良好的团队合作是什么样的呢？

sentences.en: What are the key ingredients of a highly effective team versus one that's a dysfunctional mess?
sentences.zh: 一个高效能团队与一个功能失调的烂摊子相比，核心要素是什么？

sentences.en: And what does good team training include?
sentences.zh: 良好的团队培训包含哪些内容？

sentences.en: Do you have to like your coworkers to function as an effective team?
sentences.zh: 你必须喜欢你的同事才能作为一个高效的团队运作吗？

sentences.en: Is it possible to make any team work together?
sentences.zh: 有可能让任何团队都协同工作吗？

sentences.en: Also, what are the differences between working on remote versus in-person teams?
sentences.zh: 还有，在远程团队和面对面团队中工作有什么区别？

sentences.en: Or are teamwork issues the same whether you're seeing each other in person or on Zoom?
sentences.zh: 或者，无论你是面对面见面还是通过 Zoom 交流，团队合作的问题都是一样的吗？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学聊天室》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Eduardo Salas, a professor and chair of the Department of Psychological Sciences at Rice University.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是莱斯大学心理科学系教授兼系主任爱德华多·萨拉斯博士。

sentences.en: He is an industrial organizational and human factors psychologist whose research focuses on understanding how teams work and how to design and implement effective team training strategies.
sentences.zh: 他是一名工业组织与人机工程学心理学家，其研究重点是理解团队如何运作以及如何设计和实施有效的团队培训策略。

sentences.en: Dr. Salas has co-authored more than 600 journal articles and book chapters, co-edited 33 books, and authored two books on team training and the science of teamwork.
sentences.zh: 萨拉斯博士合著了 600 多篇期刊文章和书章，合编了 33 本书，并撰写了两本关于团队培训和团队合作科学的书籍。

sentences.en: His most recent book is Teams That Work, The Seven Drivers of Team Effectiveness.
sentences.zh: 他最近的一本书是《高效团队：团队效能的七大驱动因素》。

sentences.en: Dr. Salas is an APA fellow and won APA's 2016 Award for Outstanding Lifetime Contributions to Psychology.
sentences.zh: 萨拉斯博士是美国心理学会会士，并荣获了美国心理学会 2016 年杰出终身贡献奖。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining me today, Dr. Salas.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您今天能来，萨拉斯博士。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: I'm thrilled to be here.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: You relate an anecdote at the beginning of your book where a business leader you were working with said, we don't have time for teamwork here.
sentences.zh: 你在书的开篇讲述了一个轶事：你曾合作过的一位商业领袖说：“我们这里没有时间搞团队合作。”

sentences.en: We have a business to run.
sentences.zh: “我们还有生意要做。”

sentences.en: Why is it important for organizations to think about teamwork?
sentences.zh: 为什么组织考虑团队合作如此重要？

sentences.en: And do you find that particular perspective is common?
sentences.zh: 你发现这种特定观点很常见吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So that's one of the myths out there, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这也是现存的迷思之一，对吧？

sentences.en: So in my going around the corporate world, especially most CEOs, most leaders think that they're doing a great job with teams and that they're good team players.
sentences.zh: 因此，在我走访企业界的过程中，尤其是大多数首席执行官和大多数领导者都认为他们在团队管理方面做得很好，而且自己也是优秀的团队成员。

sentences.en: However, when they learn about the science and the principles that we have to offer, all of a sudden they say, oh, wow, I didn't know that.
sentences.zh: 然而，当他们了解了我们所能提供的科学和原则时，他们突然会说：“哦，哇，我以前不知道这个。”

sentences.en: Oh, I didn't think about that.
sentences.zh: “哦，我没想过这一点。”

sentences.en: And then they try to do something different.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会尝试做出改变。

sentences.en: So some CEOs and some, again, corporate executives really don't have a good grasp about the science of teamwork and what the science of teamwork can offer.
sentences.zh: 因此，一些首席执行官和某些企业高管确实对团队合作的科学以及团队合作科学能提供什么没有很好的理解。

sentences.en: So what makes for a good, highly effective team?
sentences.zh: 那么，是什么造就了一个优秀、高效的团队？

sentences.en: What have researchers found are the key ingredients needed for a team to function well?
sentences.zh: 研究人员发现团队良好运作所需的关键要素是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, you know, in a simple way, we look for three kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，简单来说，我们寻找三种东西。

sentences.en: You know, it's the ABCs.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就是 ABC。

sentences.en: What are the attitudes?
sentences.zh: 什么是态度？

sentences.en: What are the behaviors?
sentences.zh: 什么是行为？

sentences.en: And what are the cognitions?
sentences.zh: 什么是认知？

sentences.en: So the attitudes is, right, the mindset, how the team members think about the collective activity and their motivations and their goals.
sentences.zh: 态度就是正确的思维方式，即团队成员如何看待集体活动以及他们的动机和目标。

sentences.en: The behaviors is about the role clarity, who's responsible for what, who's going to back me up, who is going to do what when.
sentences.zh: 行为关乎角色清晰度，即谁对什么负责、谁来支持我、谁将在何时做什么。

sentences.en: And the cognitions is, in general, about a shared understanding of the task, a shared understanding of the goals, a shared understanding of the mission.
sentences.zh: 而认知通常关乎对任务的共同理解、对目标的共同理解、对使命的共同理解。

sentences.en: What is it that we're trying to accomplish?
sentences.zh: 我们到底想完成什么？

sentences.en: So under these, under the ABCs, there are a set of competencies that affected teams, essentially, master.
sentences.zh: 因此，在这些 ABC 之下，有一套高效团队基本上能够掌握的能力。

sentences.en: And that's what team training does, or teamwork training of some kind.
sentences.zh: 这也是团队培训或某种形式的团队合作培训所做的事情。

sentences.en: And so we know what are the ABCs now.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在知道了 ABC 是什么。

sentences.en: And you know that in our book, with my colleague, Scott Tannenbaum, we outline seven drivers, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，在我和同事斯科特·坦嫩鲍姆合著的书里，我们列出了七大驱动因素，对吧？

sentences.en: And we invoke the seven Cs of teamwork in that book.
sentences.zh: 我们在书中援引了团队合作的七个 C。

sentences.en: So is any one of these factors more important than another?
sentences.zh: 那么，这些因素中是否有哪一个比其他因素更重要？

sentences.en: And what happens if a team is missing one of these drivers?
sentences.zh: 如果团队缺少其中一个驱动因素会发生什么？

sentences.en: Well, they're all interrelated.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它们都是相互关联的。

sentences.en: And they're built on each other, right?
sentences.zh: 并且它们是建立在彼此基础之上的，对吧？

sentences.en: So you can, in a way, can compensate one for the other.
sentences.zh: 所以，在某种程度上，你可以用一个来弥补另一个。

sentences.en: But at the end, in order to be a well-functioning team, a team that is resilient and that has good performance over time, you need all these ingredients.
sentences.zh: 但最终，为了成为一个运转良好的团队——一个具有韧性并在随时间推移中表现出色的团队——你需要所有这些要素。

sentences.en: And so what are these ingredients?
sentences.zh: 那么这些要素是什么呢？

sentences.en: So let me go through the seven Cs real quickly so that the listeners can understand.
sentences.zh: 让我快速浏览一下这七个 C，以便听众能够理解。

sentences.en: So the first C is a capability, right?
sentences.zh: 所以第一个 C 是能力（capability），对吧？

sentences.en: This is about having the right people in the team.
sentences.zh: 这关乎团队中是否有合适的人选。

sentences.en: It's about having talented, competent team members.
sentences.zh: 这关乎拥有才华横溢、胜任工作的团队成员。

sentences.en: And the first rule of teamwork really is, or one of the rules of teamwork is, you cannot be a good team member if you don't know your job.
sentences.zh: 团队合作的第一条规则——或者说团队合作的规则之一——是，如果你不懂自己的工作，你就无法成为一名优秀的团队成员。

sentences.en: And so you have to have the capability and you have to have the right mix of people.
sentences.zh: 因此，你必须具备能力，并且必须拥有合适的人员组合。

sentences.en: The second C is cooperation.
sentences.zh: 第二个 C 是合作（cooperation）。

sentences.en: Cooperation.
sentences.zh: 合作。

sentences.en: Cooperation is about a mindset.
sentences.zh: 合作关乎一种心态。

sentences.en: It's about, I like being in a team.
sentences.zh: 它意味着：我喜欢身处团队中。

sentences.en: I want to be in a team.
sentences.zh: 我想加入团队。

sentences.en: I seek the input from others.
sentences.zh: 我征求他人的意见。

sentences.en: And I value the input from others.
sentences.zh: 并且我重视他人的意见。

sentences.en: The third C is coordination.
sentences.zh: 第三个 C 是协调（coordination）。

sentences.en: And coordination is about the behaviors.
sentences.zh: 协调关乎行为。

sentences.en: Again, who is going to back me up?
sentences.zh: 同样，谁来支持我？

sentences.en: Who's going to help me?
sentences.zh: 谁来帮我？

sentences.en: And who's going to do what?
sentences.zh: 谁来做什么？

sentences.en: And it's really about role clarity.
sentences.zh: 它实际上关乎角色清晰度。

sentences.en: The next thing is about cognition.
sentences.zh: 接下来是认知（cognition）。

sentences.en: And cognition is about the shared understanding of the task, right?
sentences.zh: 认知关乎对任务的共同理解，对吧？

sentences.en: So it's the shared knowledge that we have as a team in order to execute a task.
sentences.zh: 所以它是我们作为一个团队为了执行任务而拥有的共同知识。

sentences.en: Then you have communication.
sentences.zh: 然后是沟通（communication）。

sentences.en: Communication is, the way we describe it, is really about the information exchange protocols, right?
sentences.zh: 我们对沟通的描述，实际上关乎信息交换协议，对吧？

sentences.en: It's about the terminology, the clarity of the terminology, the timeliness of the information.
sentences.zh: 它关乎术语、术语的清晰度以及信息的及时性。

sentences.en: And then you have coaching.
sentences.zh: 接下来是执教（coaching）。

sentences.en: The way I describe this is, you know, coaching is about the team leaders.
sentences.zh: 我对此的描述是，你知道，执教关乎团队领导者。

sentences.en: And what we want our team leaders to act, in a sense, is like good coaches.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，我们希望团队领导者的行为像优秀的教练。

sentences.en: So what do good coaches do?
sentences.zh: 那么优秀的教练会做什么？

sentences.en: They promote teamwork, right?
sentences.zh: 他们促进团队合作，对吧？

sentences.en: They care about the team members.
sentences.zh: 他们关心团队成员。

sentences.en: They develop them.
sentences.zh: 他们培养团队成员。

sentences.en: And so that's what we want team leaders to act as good coaches.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们希望团队领导者充当优秀教练的原因。

sentences.en: And the final C is conditions.
sentences.zh: 最后一个 C 是条件（conditions）。

sentences.en: And this is about the organizational conditions.
sentences.zh: 这关乎组织条件。

sentences.en: It's a similar word, similar term to culture.
sentences.zh: 这是一个与文化（culture）相似的词，类似的术语。

sentences.en: So this is about the incentives, the reinforcements that leadership, that top leadership puts in the organization to support teamwork.
sentences.zh: 所以这关乎领导层、高层领导在组织中为支持团队合作而设立的激励措施和强化机制。

sentences.en: So, you know, in these seven Cs, it's really not a model or a theory, just a heuristic to organize the body of knowledge that we have under these things.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这七个 C 实际上不是一个模型或理论，而只是一种启发法，用来组织我们在这些方面拥有的知识体系。

sentences.en: So effective teams have, in a sense, managed the Cs, especially the first six Cs, right?
sentences.zh: 因此，高效团队在某种程度上掌握了这些 C，尤其是前六个 C，对吧？

sentences.en: And the last one being conditions.
sentences.zh: 最后一个则是条件。

sentences.en: So, you know, they have the right people.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，他们拥有合适的人选。

sentences.en: They have role clarity.
sentences.zh: 他们具备清晰的角色定位。

sentences.en: They have a shared understanding of the task.
sentences.zh: 他们对任务有共同的理解。

sentences.en: They have robust information exchange protocols.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有强大的信息交换协议。

sentences.en: And they work under conditions that are supportive of teamwork.
sentences.zh: 并且他们在支持团队合作的条件下工作。

sentences.en: So in general, that's how this works.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，这就是它的运作方式。

sentences.en: So what happens if you are handed a team or you are put on a team and you don't really have a lot of power around the selection of who the team members are?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果你被交托一个团队，或者被安插到一个团队中，而你对于挑选团队成员并没有太大的话语权，会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: What can you do as a person who either inherits or is placed on a team if you're seeing that some of these Cs are not being followed to the letter, so to speak?
sentences.zh: 如果你发现这些 C 中有些并没有被严格遵守（可以说是形同虚设），作为继承或被安置进团队的人，你能做些什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, so, you know, there are a number of tools that you can use.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以，你知道，你可以使用许多工具。

sentences.en: You know, in our science, we have uncovered the teams that pre-brief, pre-brief, perform and debrief, outperform those that don't.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在我们的科学研究中，我们发现进行会前简报（pre-brief）、执行、以及会后总结（debrief）的团队，其表现优于不这样做的团队。

sentences.en: So, pre-briefing is basically, you know, you just join this team or this team is a little disjointed.
sentences.zh: 所以，会前简报基本上就是，你知道，你刚加入这个团队，或者这个团队有点散漫。

sentences.en: Then, okay, before we perform, before, like pilots do, before they go to the cockpit or before the flight, they pre-brief.
sentences.zh: 那么，好吧，在我们执行任务之前，就像飞行员在进入驾驶舱或飞行前所做的那样，他们会进行会前简报。

sentences.en: And they talk about, okay, where are we headed?
sentences.zh: 他们会讨论，好吧，我们的方向是什么？

sentences.en: You know, how are we going to communicate?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们将如何沟通？

sentences.en: Who's going to do what?
sentences.zh: 谁将做什么？

sentences.en: So, you know, this pre-briefing, if you have the chance to do that, allows you to clarify roles, to get an idea of who's going to do what, who has what knowledge,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，如果你有机会这样做，这种会前简报能让你澄清角色，了解谁将做什么、谁拥有什么知识、

sentences.en: who has what expertise, how are we going to communicate?
sentences.zh: 谁拥有什么专业技能，我们将如何沟通？

sentences.en: And then you perform, right?
sentences.zh: 然后你再去执行，对吧？

sentences.en: You do the task.
sentences.zh: 你完成任务。

sentences.en: It could be an hour, three hours, a few days, a month, whatever.
sentences.zh: 这可能是一个小时、三个小时、几天、一个月，随便多长时间。

sentences.en: But at some point, you need to debrief.
sentences.zh: 但在某个时刻，你需要进行会后总结。

sentences.en: And debriefing, like my colleague, Scott Tannenbaum says, you know, is the most powerful, simple intervention, yet underutilized to learn and to improve.
sentences.zh: 正如我的同事斯科特·坦嫩鲍姆所说，会后总结是最有力、最简单却又未被充分利用的学习和改进干预措施。

sentences.en: So, the debriefing is a reflection on what just happened.
sentences.zh: 因此，会后总结是对刚刚发生的事情的反思。

sentences.en: And in that reflection, usually you need to, what usually happens is you try to understand what things you need to improve, what things didn't go well,
sentences.zh: 在反思中，通常你需要做的是，通常发生的情况是，你试图了解你需要改进哪些事情、哪些事情进展不顺利，

sentences.en: and what things you need to change.
sentences.zh: 以及你需要改变哪些事情。

sentences.en: And so, this cycle, again, of pre-briefing, performing, debriefing is usually a good discipline that allows you to,
sentences.zh: 所以，这个会前简报、执行、会后总结的循环，再次证明是一种良好的纪律，它能让你——

sentences.en: even when you have a bad team or you just inherit a team that is not so good, allows you, it gives you the opportunity if you can do this discipline.
sentences.zh: 即使当你拥有一个糟糕的团队，或者你只是接手了一个不太好的团队时，只要你能遵循这种纪律，它也允许并为你提供了机会。

sentences.en: If there's a, if you can, this cycle, allows you to learn and to improve and to get, you will, the team in line.
sentences.zh: 如果你能做到这一点，这个循环就能让你学习、进步，并使团队走上正轨。

sentences.en: Now, you've worked in some industries where it's been a challenge to get the leaders to embrace your scientific theories around teamwork.
sentences.zh: 现在，你曾在一些行业工作过，在这些行业中，让领导者接受你关于团队合作的科学理论一直是一个挑战。

sentences.en: I'm thinking, whether that's pilots or in hospitals and emergency rooms, places like that.
sentences.zh: 我在想，无论是飞行员还是医院和急诊室，诸如此类的地方。

sentences.en: And then you've, you've run into resistance.
sentences.zh: 然后你遇到了阻力。

sentences.en: How have you dealt with that?
sentences.zh: 你是如何应对的？

sentences.en: Why have some industries been more resistant than others?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些行业比其他行业表现出更大的抗拒？

sentences.en: So, I started in, working in aviation a long time ago, 30 years or so ago.
sentences.zh: 所以，我很久以前开始涉足航空业工作，大约 30 年前左右。

sentences.en: And at the beginning, pilots were resistant as well, right?
sentences.zh: 起初，飞行员也是抗拒的，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, in the early 80s, it was about the right stuff, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，在 80 年代初，那讲究的是“真正的人才”（right stuff），对吧？

sentences.en: You know, and pilots were more egotistical to some degree.
sentences.zh: 你知道，而且飞行员在某种程度上更加自负。

sentences.en: However, they soon realized that when the plane goes down, they go down with the plane.
sentences.zh: 然而，他们很快意识到，当飞机坠毁时，他们也会和飞机一起坠毁。

sentences.en: And so, they had to engage.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们不得不参与进来。

sentences.en: And so, 30 years later, I mean, just about all the airlines, whether they're passenger or cargo, really embrace team training and teamwork.
sentences.zh: 因此，30 年后，我的意思是，几乎所有的航空公司，无论是客运还是货运，都真正拥抱了团队培训和团队合作。

sentences.en: They call it the CRM, crew resource management.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为 CRM，即机组资源管理。

sentences.en: And the FAA supports that and so forth.
sentences.zh: 美国联邦航空管理局（FAA）也支持这一点，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But so, this generation of pilots completely embraces, in general, the concept.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，这一代的飞行员完全接受了这个概念。

sentences.en: In healthcare, for example, you don't have that hook, right?
sentences.zh: 例如，在医疗保健领域，你没有那种“强力钩子”，对吧？

sentences.en: So, when the patient goes down, unfortunately, only the patient goes down.
sentences.zh: 所以，当患者病情恶化时，不幸的是，只有患者病情恶化。

sentences.en: And so, it's taking the healthcare, it's taking healthcare a lot longer to engage.
sentences.zh: 因此，医疗保健行业需要花费更长的时间来参与其中。

sentences.en: And the pressure really has come from, you know, the patient safety movement, the number of errors, medical errors that we still have.
sentences.zh: 而压力实际上来自于患者安全运动，以及我们仍然存在的医疗差错的数量。

sentences.en: And really, a bottoms-up approach, you know, the nurses, the technicians, the people who really, quote-unquote, touch patients, see the need to do things better for the patient.
sentences.zh: 而且说实话，这种自下而上的方式，你知道的，护士、技术人员，那些真正所谓“接触”患者的人，最能看出为患者把事情做好的必要性。

sentences.en: And little by little, kind of like one team at a time in healthcare, now, while there's still some resistance, it's a lot less than it was 20 years ago.
sentences.zh: 然后一点一点地，在医疗领域基本上就像是一个团队接一个团队，现在，虽然仍然存在一些阻力，但比20年少多了。

sentences.en: And the resistance comes from, I see it from two angles.
sentences.zh: 而且这些阻力来自哪里，我从两个角度来看。

sentences.en: One angle is a financial angle, which most CEOs, chief financial officers, and so forth worry about is, if I'm going to invest in team training,
sentences.zh: 一个角度是财务角度，大多数首席执行官、首席财务官等等所担心的是，如果我要投资团队培训，

sentences.en: what is it that I'm going to get for that investment?
sentences.zh: 我能从这笔投资中得到什么？

sentences.en: And it wasn't until recently that we were able really to answer that question when we've done a number of team training evaluations,
sentences.zh: 直到最近，当我们做了大量的团队培训评估后，我们才真正能够回答这个问题，

sentences.en: meta-analyses that really show the boost that you get out of team training.
sentences.zh: 元分析真正显示了你从团队培训中获得的提升。

sentences.en: And so, now we can answer that.
sentences.zh: 所以，现在我们可以回答这个问题了。

sentences.en: So, we say there's value and there's a performance improvement if you deploy teamwork, this is the benefit you get.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们说如果部署团队合作，就会有价值和绩效提升，这就是你获得的好处。

sentences.en: And in healthcare, we have been able to show that, to some degree, that hospitals that deploy teamwork training versus those that don't,
sentences.zh: 在医疗领域，我们在某种程度上已经能够证明，与不部署团队合作培训的医院相比，部署团队合作培训的医院，

sentences.en: medical error is reduced and mortality is reduced.
sentences.zh: 医疗差错减少了，死亡率也降低了。

sentences.en: So, there's a link, you know, between teamwork and saving lives.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，团队合作与拯救生命之间存在着联系。

sentences.en: So, that has been one.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是其中之一。

sentences.en: And the second, my opinion, at least in my experience of doing this for a long time now, is if they buy that they have to deploy teamwork training, they don't know how to do it.
sentences.zh: 第二个，在我看来，至少在我长期从事这方面工作的经验中，如果他们相信必须部署团队合作培训，他们却不知道该怎么做。

sentences.en: They don't know how to implement it.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道如何实施。

sentences.en: They don't know how to make sure that the sustainability of the behaviors that the people, the new behaviors and cognitions and attitudes that the staff just got.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道如何确保员工刚刚获得的那些行为、新行为、认知和态度的可持续性。

sentences.en: And so, you know, it takes them some time to get traction to create the conditions, one of the Cs, to create the conditions such that people perceive teamwork is important,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，他们需要花一些时间来获得推动力，以创造条件——其中一个要素——创造这样一种条件：人们认为团队合作很重要，

sentences.en: it's reinforced, it, you know, it improves patient safety, it improves patient care, and so forth.
sentences.zh: 它得到了强化，你知道的，它改善了患者安全，改善了患者护理，等等。

sentences.en: So, there have been those two lines, you know, is team training, what's the ROI, return on investment from team training,
sentences.zh: 所以，一直有这两条线，你知道的，就是团队培训，它的ROI是什么，也就是团队培训的投资回报率，

sentences.en: and then how do we roll this out so that it's sustainable over a period of time and not just, you know, a one-time event.
sentences.zh: 然后我们如何推广它，使其在一段时间内具有可持续性，而不仅仅是一个你知道的一次性事件。

sentences.en: So, what does effective team training look like and how can a company or another organization tell if their team training is actually working?
sentences.zh: 那么，有效的团队培训是什么样的，公司或其他组织如何判断他们的团队培训是否真的在起作用？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, first of all, there are several models out there in the industry, you know, that the medical community created a team training program called Team Steps with double P,
sentences.zh: 所以，首先，业界有几种模型，你知道的，医疗界创造了一个名为“Team Steps”的团队培训项目，两个P，

sentences.en: one word together.
sentences.zh: 连在一起的一个词。

sentences.en: And to simplify, any training, not only team training, but any training at the end of the day does four things.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，任何培训，不仅是团队培训，归根结底任何培训都有四个作用。

sentences.en: It gives you information, demonstration of good behaviors, bad behaviors, gives you opportunity to practice, and you get feedback.
sentences.zh: 它为你提供信息、良好行为和不良行为的示范、实践的机会，并且你还能得到反馈。

sentences.en: So, information, demonstration, practice, and feedback.
sentences.zh: 所以，信息、示范、实践和反馈。

sentences.en: So, these Team Steps and other systems that are out there, by and large, have those four components, right?
sentences.zh: 因此，这些Team Steps以及业界存在的其他系统，大体上都具备这四个组成部分，对吧？

sentences.en: And so, you learn about the team principles, you look at videos of good teams and bad teams, and you can analyze them and, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，你了解团队原则，你观看优秀团队和糟糕团队的视频，你可以分析它们，并且，你知道的，

sentences.en: extract what's good and bad about each of these video tapes, for example.
sentences.zh: 比如提炼出这些录像中各自的好与坏。

sentences.en: Then you get opportunities to practice, you might role play, you might use a simulation, and so forth, and then you get feedback on that.
sentences.zh: 然后你获得实践的机会，你可能会进行角色扮演，可能会使用模拟等等，然后你会得到关于这些的反馈。

sentences.en: So, training or team training that has those four elements have a higher probability of transfer of training.
sentences.zh: 因此，具备这四个要素的培训或团队培训，其培训迁移的概率更高。

sentences.en: In other words, the people will apply the skills they just learned back to the job.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，人们会将刚学到的技能应用回工作中。

sentences.en: However, you know, just deploying team training, you know, it's really not enough.
sentences.zh: 然而，你知道的，仅仅部署团队培训，其实是不够的。

sentences.en: There is a science of training as well.
sentences.zh: 培训也是一门科学。

sentences.en: In the science of training, it tells us that there are things that you need to worry about after you, before you deploy the training and after you deploy the training.
sentences.zh: 培训科学告诉我们，在部署培训之前和部署培训之后，有些事情是需要你关注的。

sentences.en: So, before you deploy the training, you need to prepare the organization for the training.
sentences.zh: 因此，在部署培训之前，你需要为培训做好组织准备。

sentences.en: You train supervisors, you make sure everybody's on board to that.
sentences.zh: 你培训主管，确保每个人都对此达成共识。

sentences.en: And actually, most team training or most training fails because the organization is not ready to receive the training.
sentences.zh: 事实上，大多数团队培训或绝大多数培训之所以失败，是因为组织还没有准备好接受培训。

sentences.en: So, and then you have to worry about afterwards, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，接下来你还得关注事后，对吧？

sentences.en: Are you supportive of the skills, the competencies that the people just got?
sentences.zh: 你是否支持人们刚刚获得的那些技能和能力？

sentences.en: Do you reinforce that?
sentences.zh: 你是否对此进行强化？

sentences.en: Do you give them an opportunity to perform?
sentences.zh: 你是否给他们提供表现的机会？

sentences.en: Do you, you know, measure them, this new company?
sentences.zh: 你是否，你知道的，去衡量他们，这个新团队？

sentences.en: So, long story is good team training.
sentences.zh: 所以，长话短说，这就是好的团队培训。

sentences.en: You need to worry about things that you do before the team training, things you do during the team training, which I just explained, the information demonstration practice,
sentences.zh: 你需要关注团队培训前要做的事情，团队培训中要做的事情——也就是我刚才解释的信息、示范、实践，

sentences.en: and things that you do after training.
sentences.zh: 以及培训后要做的事情。

sentences.en: Now, there have been many evaluations of medical team training and other team training, and two or three meta-analyses, and for the audience,
sentences.zh: 现在，对医疗团队培训和其他团队培训已经进行了很多评估，有两到三个元分析，对于观众来说，

sentences.en: the meta-analysis and integration of many findings, a quantitative integration of many findings.
sentences.zh: 元分析就是对许多研究结果的综合，是对许多研究结果的定量综合。

sentences.en: But this meta-analyses clearly show the benefit of team training.
sentences.zh: 但这些元分析清楚地显示了团队培训的好处。

sentences.en: You know, it boosts performance, reduces errors, people are more engaged, people are more satisfied.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它提升了绩效，减少了差错，人们的参与度更高，满意度也更高。

sentences.en: So, how important are individual differences, such as personalities, in determining how well a team works together?
sentences.zh: 那么，诸如个性之类的个体差异，在决定团队合作的好坏方面有多重要？

sentences.en: I mean, are there really some people who just aren't team players, or can pretty much any group of personalities be instructed, taught how to work together?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，真的有些人就是不适合团队合作吗，还是说几乎任何个性组合都可以被指导、教导如何一起工作？

sentences.en: Yeah, the easiest example I have is most of us, well, not most of us, all of us, have a disposition.
sentences.zh: 是的，我能举出的最简单的例子是，我们大多数人——嗯，不是大多数人，是我们所有人，都有某种倾向。

sentences.en: Either we're collective-oriented, or we are egocentric.
sentences.zh: 要么我们是集体导向的，要么我们是唯我独尊的。

sentences.en: If you're collective-oriented, you like being in teams, you want to be in teams, and again, you seek and value the input from others.
sentences.zh: 如果你是集体导向的，你喜欢在团队中，你想在团队中，同样地，你会寻求并重视来自他人的输入。

sentences.en: The egocentric disposition are the long walls, people who don't engage in collective activity, no matter what you do.
sentences.zh: 唯我独尊的倾向就是孤狼，无论你做什么都不参与集体活动的人。

sentences.en: So, in teams, you need people who are collective-oriented.
sentences.zh: 所以，在团队中，你需要集体导向的人。

sentences.en: You know, I'll give you a sports example that I love to use.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我举一个我喜欢用的体育例子。

sentences.en: So, Michael Jordan, you know, one of the greatest basketball players ever.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·乔丹，你知道的，史上最伟大的篮球运动员之一。

sentences.en: In his biography, he acknowledges that, you know, when he was part of the Chicago Bulls, it wasn't until, he says, until he was,
sentences.zh: 在他的自传中，他承认，你知道的，当他是芝加哥公牛队的一员时，直到他说，

sentences.en: it wasn't until we got Scotty Pippen in the pools that we began to win championships.
sentences.zh: 直到我们在公牛队得到了斯科蒂·皮蓬，我们才开始赢得总冠军。

sentences.en: And those, in the audience who doesn't know about Scotty Pippen, he's a retired player now, but he was a great defensive player.
sentences.zh: 而对于观众中不知道斯科蒂·皮蓬是谁的人，他现在是一名退役球员，但他曾是一名伟大的防守球员。

sentences.en: Not a high scorer, but he had the most assists.
sentences.zh: 得分不高，但他拥有最多的助攻。

sentences.en: He passed the ball a lot.
sentences.zh: 他经常传球。

sentences.en: And so, in the sense, he was collective-oriented.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种意义上，他是集体导向的。

sentences.en: So, the star of the team needed somebody that would pass the ball.
sentences.zh: 所以，团队的明星需要一个愿意传球的人。

sentences.en: So, in teams, you need that.
sentences.zh: 因此，在团队中，你需要这样的人。

sentences.en: You need somebody who's going to be passing the ball.
sentences.zh: 你需要一个会传球的人。

sentences.en: And so, that is a disposition that you need to have.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一种你需要具备的倾向。

sentences.en: Now, there's some research, however, that shows that egocentric individuals, under some circumstances, engage in collective activity.
sentences.zh: 不过，也有一些研究表明，唯我独尊的个人在某些情况下也会参与集体活动。

sentences.en: And when those factors are no longer there, then they go back to being egocentric.
sentences.zh: 而当这些因素不复存在时，他们又会恢复到唯我独尊的状态。

sentences.en: So, you just have to find what are those conditions.
sentences.zh: 所以，你只需要找出这些条件是什么。

sentences.en: Now, many people have made the switch to working remotely in the past three years.
sentences.zh: 过去三年里，许多人都转为远程办公。

sentences.en: Are there big differences between working on remote teams versus in-person teams?
sentences.zh: 远程团队工作与面对面团队工作之间有很大的区别吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 有。

sentences.en: The biggest challenge is making connections, in my view, to simplify things.
sentences.zh: 依我之见，简而言之，最大的挑战是建立联系。

sentences.en: So, we started this discussion by talking about the ABCs, the attitudes, behaviors, and cognitions.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们从讨论ABC开始，即态度（Attitudes）、行为（Behaviors）和认知（Cognitions）。

sentences.en: So, in remote, in a remote setting, or even in Zoom, you know, how do you keep those connections, the behaviors, the cognitions, and the attitudes?
sentences.zh: 因此，在远程环境中，甚至在Zoom中，你知道的，你如何保持这些联系、行为、认知和态度？

sentences.en: It's quite challenging.
sentences.zh: 这相当具有挑战性。

sentences.en: And, you know, how do you keep the trust, right?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，如何保持信任，对吧？

sentences.en: And so, in a sense, the science helps you, helps co-located teams and distributed teams or teams that don't see each other, in a way.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，科学可以帮助你，在某种程度上帮助同地协作的团队、分布式团队或者互不见面的团队。

sentences.en: It's just that sometimes some of the Cs are more important and more challenging when you are distributed.
sentences.zh: 只是有时当你处于分布式环境中时，某些C要素会更加重要也更具挑战性。

sentences.en: The biggest problem or the biggest challenge that distributed teams have, or hybrid teams, is truSt.
sentences.zh: 分布式团队或混合团队面临的最大问题或最大挑战就是信任。

sentences.en: How do I, how do you, this mutual truSt.
sentences.zh: 我该如何……你们该如何建立这种相互信任。

sentences.en: And mutual trust is needed so that you can have some psychological safety, which is psychological safety is the license that you have to speak up, right?
sentences.zh: 我们需要相互信任，以便能够拥有一定的心理安全感，而心理安全感就是你敢于直言不讳的许可，对吧？

sentences.en: And very quickly, you know, all teams, sooner or later, engage in conflict.
sentences.zh: 很快你就会发现，你知道的，所有团队迟早都会陷入冲突。

sentences.en: And one way to resolve conflict is the psychological safety.
sentences.zh: 解决冲突的方法之一就是心理安全感。

sentences.en: You have to be able to have hard, difficult conversations about something without any repercussions.
sentences.zh: 你必须能够毫无后顾之忧地就某些事情进行艰难的、困难的对话。

sentences.en: So, that's the difficulty in distributed teams or teams that don't see each other.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是分布式团队或互不见面的团队的难点所在。

sentences.en: How do they create this little trust so they can get to know each other?
sentences.zh: 他们如何建立这种微小的信任以便能够相互了解？

sentences.en: I've seen examples where, in banks, for example, when they have teams that are distributed over the world, they try to create events.
sentences.zh: 我见过一些例子，比如在银行里，当他们的团队分布在世界各地时，他们会试图创造一些活动。

sentences.en: They call this the water cooler event, right?
sentences.zh: 他们称之为饮水机活动，对吧？

sentences.en: So, when you go to the water cooler, you have a, you know, a 10, 5-minute conversation with your teammate about something that has nothing to do with the job, maybe, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，当你去饮水机旁时，你可能会和队友进行一场持续10分钟、5分钟的对话，谈论一些可能与工作毫无关系的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, what did you do this weekend?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你这个周末做了什么？

sentences.en: My kid is doing that, that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 我的孩子在做那个，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: So, these teams try to create this water cooler event.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些团队试图创造这种饮水机活动。

sentences.en: And I've seen them, for example, when they, one of the banks that I've helped, Monday mornings when they have the first meeting, they take turns around the team.
sentences.zh: 我见过他们这样做，例如，在我帮助过的一家银行里，周一早上的第一次会议上，他们会轮流发言。

sentences.en: And each, one of the members always takes about five minutes, and that's all, five minutes, to talk about their kids or what did they do during the weekend.
sentences.zh: 每个成员总是花大约五分钟时间——就五分钟——谈论他们的孩子或者他们在周末做了什么。

sentences.en: And something like that, to kind of like, to break the ice a little bit, but also to learn about you.
sentences.zh: 类似这样的话题，有点像是打破僵局，同时也是为了了解你。

sentences.en: And then, over time, it creates the stress.
sentences.zh: 然后，随着时间的推移，这就建立了信任。

sentences.en: What about, there are places, for example, where you can go and do team building exercises, ropes courses, things like that.
sentences.zh: 那么，有些地方，你可以去进行团队建设练习，比如绳索课程之类的，怎么样？

sentences.en: I mean, are those, that sounds similar to the water cooler idea, but a little different in that, you know, you're really outside of the workplace.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，听起来这类似于饮水机的主意，但有点不同，因为你确实身处工作场所之外。

sentences.en: And you might be doing something that looks like it could be a little bit perilous,
sentences.zh: 而且你可能在做一些看起来有点危险的事情，

sentences.en: and you might have to depend on one of your coworkers to make sure that you don't fall on your face.
sentences.zh: 你可能不得不依赖某个同事来确保自己不会脸朝下摔倒。

sentences.en: Does that make for a more effective team?
sentences.zh: 这能造就一个更高效的团队吗？

sentences.en: Or is this just sort of, you know, we're really just having fun, and then we're going to go back and be a bad team, the same that we were before?
sentences.zh: 还是这仅仅意味着，你知道的，我们其实只是在玩乐，然后回去之后依然是个糟糕的团队，跟以前一样？

sentences.en: Well, let me tell you the story.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我给你讲个故事。

sentences.en: So, there's a difference between team building and team training, in my mind.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，团队建设和团队培训是有区别的。

sentences.en: Team training is about getting team competencies, you know, the C's or the ABC's that I talked about.
sentences.zh: 团队培训是关于获得团队能力的，你知道的，就是我谈到的那些C要素或ABC。

sentences.en: So, it's about team competencies.
sentences.zh: 所以，它是关于团队能力的。

sentences.en: Team building is like you just described.
sentences.zh: 团队建设就像你刚才描述的那样。

sentences.en: You know, you go into the wilderness of North Carolina somewhere, and you're wine and dine for three days, and you do tasks, and then do the job.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你去了北卡罗来纳州的某个荒野，在那里好吃好喝三天，做做任务，然后再回去工作。

sentences.en: That's really about role clarity, the biggest benefit of that.
sentences.zh: 那其实是关于明确角色的，这是它最大的好处。

sentences.en: Because during those three days, again, you're wine and dine with your teammate, and along that way, you're going to talk about what each other is, what you do,
sentences.zh: 因为在那三天里，同样地，你和队友一起吃喝，在这个过程中，你们会谈论彼此是谁、你们做什么，

sentences.en: and you're going to learn about that.
sentences.zh: 然后你会了解这些。

sentences.en: So, about almost 20 years ago, maybe it needs to be updated.
sentences.zh: 所以，差不多20年前吧，也许现在需要更新了。

sentences.en: I did a meta-analysis of, again, a quantitative integration of team building.
sentences.zh: 我也做过关于团队建设的元分析，同样是对团队建设的定量综合。

sentences.en: And I found very little correlation with performance, which a lot of consultants didn't like.
sentences.zh: 我发现它与绩效的关系微乎其微，这让很多顾问不太高兴。

sentences.en: But there's a benefit of team building.
sentences.zh: 但团队建设确实有它的好处。

sentences.en: You know, you get this role clarity.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你能获得这种角色清晰度。

sentences.en: You learn more about your teammates and so forth.
sentences.zh: 你对队友有了更多的了解等等。

sentences.en: But team training is about competencies.
sentences.zh: 但团队培训是关于能力的。

sentences.en: It's very different.
sentences.zh: 这是非常不同的。

sentences.en: So, the two have a place.
sentences.zh: 所以，这两者都有其价值所在。

sentences.en: It's just that you need to make sure that you understand the benefits of each one.
sentences.zh: 只是你需要确保自己理解各自的好处。

sentences.en: I want to ask you how your background in the military influenced your work as a psychologist and in your interest in teaMs.
sentences.zh: 我想问你，你的军事背景是如何影响你作为一名心理学家以及你对团队的兴趣的？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So, I worked for the Navy for 15 years, and I was hired to develop a team performance laboratory at that time.
sentences.zh: 所以，我在海军工作了15年，当时受雇去建立一个团队绩效实验室。

sentences.en: And interestingly enough, in order to do that, with my colleagues that I recruited and students, what we needed to do is immerse ourselves in the context where the Marines, airmen,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，为了做到这一点，我和我招募的同事以及学生们，我们需要做的是让自己沉浸在海军陆战队员、空军人员、

sentences.en: women were performing.
sentences.zh: 女性执行任务的环境中。

sentences.en: So, what I learned working for the military was that in order to help, in order to understand what the teams do and the help they need, I needed to learn the context,
sentences.zh: 所以，我在军队工作中学到的是，为了提供帮助，为了理解团队在做什么以及他们需要什么帮助，我需要了解具体情境，

sentences.en: embed myself in what they do.
sentences.zh: 把自己融入他们所做的事情中。

sentences.en: So, the beauty, one of the most satisfying things in my career over the last almost 40 years now is that when I go and try to help organizations,
sentences.zh: 所以，在过去近40年的职业生涯中，最美妙、最令人满意的的事情之一就是，当我试图去帮助组织时，

sentences.en: I embed myself and my colleagues in the context and learn, you know, we sweat with them, we wake up early, we stay late, whatever the demand is.
sentences.zh: 我和同事们会把自己融入到具体情境中去学习，你知道的，我们和他们一起流汗，早起，晚归，无论有什么需求。

sentences.en: And I learned that in the military early on, that when you sweat with them, then they listen to you and they respect you.
sentences.zh: 我在早年的军旅生涯中就学到这一点，当你和他们一起流汗时，他们就会听你的，尊重你。

sentences.en: You're not this ivory tower professor or whatever researcher doing things.
sentences.zh: 你不是那种纸上谈兵的象牙塔教授或是做研究的研究人员。

sentences.en: And so, when I left working for the Navy in 1999 or so, I took that with me and said, you know, if I'm going to learn, I've done work with air traffic controllers,
sentences.zh: 所以，当我在1999年左右离开海军时，我把这些带上了，心想，你知道的，如果我要学习——我跟空中交通管制员合作过，

sentences.en: I've done work in healthcare, for banks, for NASA, I mean, you know, oil and gas.
sentences.zh: 我在医疗领域、银行、NASA工作过，我的意思是，你知道的，还有石油和天然气领域。

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，

sentences.en: I've embedded myself and then learn and then you can contextualize then the interventions and then use the psychological principles that we know to adapt to their environment.
sentences.zh: 我让自己沉浸其中去学习，然后你就可以将干预措施情境化，接着运用我们所知的心理学原理来适应他们的环境。

sentences.en: And it has a tremendous impact because they get it.
sentences.zh: 这会产生巨大的影响，因为他们能理解。

sentences.en: It's their context, but, you know, but the psychological principles that we use kind of cross all these industries, by the way, it's just that you contextualize them.
sentences.zh: 这是他们的情境，但是，你知道的，顺便说一句，我们使用的心理学原理贯穿了所有这些行业，只是你需要将它们情境化。

sentences.en: So, that's what I learned in the military.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是我在军队学到的东西。

sentences.en: It's, you know, I call it sweating with them.
sentences.zh: 这就是，你知道的，我称之为和他们一起流汗。

sentences.en: What happens if a team falls into conflict and gets stuck and it really doesn't seem to be working effectively?
sentences.zh: 如果一个团队陷入冲突并陷入僵局，似乎无法有效运作，会发生什么？

sentences.en: Are there some techniques that can be applied to fix it or do you just blow it up and say, this team is just not going to cut it?
sentences.zh: 有没有什么技术可以应用来解决它，还是说你直接把它解散，然后说，这个团队就是不行？

sentences.en: Well, coaching is one, you know, if you can get an external view.
sentences.zh: 嗯，辅导是一种方法，你知道的，如果你能获得外部的视角。

sentences.en: Another way is, you know, I learned this from my colleague, Scott Tannema, again, you know, there's a technique.
sentences.zh: 另一种方法是，你知道的，这是我从我的同事斯科特·坦纳马那里学到的，同样地，有一种技术。

sentences.en: If you can engage in a technique to self-diagnose, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你能运用某种技术来进行自我诊断，对吧？

sentences.en: So, you usually ask maybe three questions, you know, as a team, what things we need to stop doing?
sentences.zh: 通常你们大概会提三个问题，作为一个团队，有哪些事情是我们需要停止做的？

sentences.en: As a team, what things we need to start doing?
sentences.zh: 作为一个团队，有哪些事情是我们需要开始做的？

sentences.en: And as a team, what things we need to improve?
sentences.zh: 作为一个团队，有哪些事情是我们需要改进的？

sentences.en: So, if you have psychological safety and you can speak up, then you do this diagnosis of your team, stop, start, continue.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你具备心理安全感并且敢于直言，你就可以对你的团队进行这种诊断：停止、开始、继续。

sentences.en: You'll find out what's wrong and what's creating the conflict and what things we need to do to ensure that we don't get into this mode.
sentences.zh: 你会发现哪里出了问题，是什么引发了冲突，以及我们需要采取什么措施来确保我们不会陷入这种状态。

sentences.en: So, there are techniques.
sentences.zh: 所以，是有技巧的。

sentences.en: It's just, again, you have to have the discipline of, okay, let's talk about this, right?
sentences.zh: 这只是说，同样地，你必须有这种纪律，好吧，我们来谈谈这个，对吧？

sentences.en: Let's get serious.
sentences.zh: 我们认真点。

sentences.en: The team is not functioning well.
sentences.zh: 团队运作得不好。

sentences.en: You know, we're not taking care of the patient.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们没有照顾好患者。

sentences.en: We're not doing whatever.
sentences.zh: 我们没有做好某些事情。

sentences.en: You know, we're exhibiting unsafe behavior.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们表现出了不安全的行为。

sentences.en: We need to do something.
sentences.zh: 我们需要采取行动了。

sentences.en: So, time out.
sentences.zh: 所以，暂停一下。

sentences.en: Let's talk about this.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈这个。

sentences.en: And then you say, okay, we need to stop doing this, start, continue.
sentences.zh: 然后你会说，好吧，我们需要停止这样做、开始这样做、继续这样做。

sentences.en: Does every team to be effective have to have a designated leader or is that a role that can shift as the team does its work?
sentences.zh: 为了保持高效，每个团队都必须有一个指定的领导者，还是说这个角色可以随着团队的工作进展而转变？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不是的。

sentences.en: Actually, I've seen in healthcare, shared leadership is probably, it's a way to function in some teaMs.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我在医疗保健领域看到过，共享领导力可能是在某些团队中运作的一种方式。

sentences.en: You know, if you get, you know, the ORs is one example of that, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果你去看看，手术室就是一个例子，对吧？

sentences.en: At one point, the anesthesiologist is leading, then it might be the technician, and then it might be the surgeon, and then back to the anesthesiologiSt.
sentences.zh: 某个时刻是麻醉医师在领导，然后可能是技术员，然后可能是外科医师，接着又回到麻醉医师。

sentences.en: So, no, I don't, you know, more and more jobs and more and more teams have shared leadership.
sentences.zh: 所以，不，我不觉得，越来越多的工作和越来越多的团队都采用了共享领导力。

sentences.en: You know, somebody with the right expertise steps in at the right time to lead, to facilitate.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，具备合适专业知识的人会在合适的时机介入，进行领导和促进。

sentences.en: So, last question, what are you working on now?
sentences.zh: 那么最后一个问题，你现在在研究什么？

sentences.en: What are the big questions you still want to answer?
sentences.zh: 你仍然想要解答的重大问题是什么？

sentences.en: What motivates me now, after doing all this work for all these years, is what are the organizational conditions that are needed so that the behaviors, cognitions,
sentences.zh: 在做了这么多年这些研究之后，现在真正激励我的是：需要具备哪些组织条件，才能让这些行为、认知

sentences.en: and attitudes are sustained over time?
sentences.zh: 和态度随着时间推移而持续下去？

sentences.en: So, how do we create organizations?
sentences.zh: 所以，我们该如何创建组织？

sentences.en: How do we design organizations?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何设计组织？

sentences.en: How does the leadership, the C-suite, need to act, and what things they need to do in order to ensure that the behaviors, that teamwork is sustained over time,
sentences.zh: 领导层、高管层需要如何行动，他们需要做些什么来确保这些行为、团队合作能够长期持续下去，

sentences.en: and it becomes part of the DNA of the organization, right?
sentences.zh: 并成为组织基因的一部分，对吧？

sentences.en: It gets ingrained.
sentences.zh: 使其根深蒂固。

sentences.en: So, I think that's one of the biggest challenges.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这是最大的挑战之一。

sentences.en: But these days, I mean, there's all kinds of technologies going on.
sentences.zh: 但现在这个时代，各种新技术层出不穷。

sentences.en: There's, you know, there's human automation teams, there's human robo teams, there's robo-to-robo teaMs.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，有人机协作团队，有人机协作团队，有机器人与机器人的团队。

sentences.en: And so, now there are other, you know, I'm not an expert in those, but I know there's a lot of interest in this kind of teaming, right, with AI, with automation, with a robot.
sentences.zh: 因此，现在还有其他一些——虽然我不是这方面的专家，但我知道大家对这种团队合作形式非常感兴趣，对吧，涉及人工智能、自动化、机器人。

sentences.en: But, and so, that's also the kind of questions that other scientists, scholars are trying to answer, you know, how do you mimic, how do two robots mimic teamwork?
sentences.zh: 但是，这也是其他科学家、学者试图解答的问题，你知道，你如何模仿，两个机器人如何模仿团队合作？

sentences.en: All the things that I've talked about to some degree.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上就是我所谈论的所有内容。

sentences.en: And so, but to me, my, the things that interest me are those conditions and translate the science, the psychological science that we have, the principles that we have,
sentences.zh: 所以，对我而言，让我感兴趣的是那些条件，并将我们拥有的科学、心理学科学、我们拥有的原则进行转化，

sentences.en: so that people can use and apply and improve their teams and their lives and so forth and so on.
sentences.zh: 以便人们能够使用、应用并改善他们的团队、他们的生活等等。

sentences.en: So, that's what turns me on this day, is the translation.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是现阶段让我兴奋的地方，也就是转化工作。

sentences.en: Well, this is all really interesting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些真的都非常有趣。

sentences.en: I very much appreciate you taking the time to talk with us today.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您今天抽空与我们交谈。

sentences.en: Thank you, Dr. Silas.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，赛拉斯博士。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: You can find previous episodes of Speaking of Psychology on our website at www.speakingofpsychology.org or on Apple, Stitcher, YouTube, or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 您可以在我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology.org 或在 Apple、Stitcher、YouTube 以及您获取播客的任何平台上找到《心理学话你知》(Speaking of Psychology) 往期的节目。

sentences.en: And again, we'd like to hear from you about what you think of this podcast and what you'd like us to talk about more than we are now.
sentences.zh: 再次重申，我们很想听听您对这档播客的看法，以及您希望我们多聊些什么话题。

sentences.en: So, please go to our website, speakingofpsychology.org, and look for a link to our listener survey.
sentences.zh: 因此，请访问我们的网站 speakingofpsychology.org，寻找我们听众调查的链接。

sentences.en: If you have comments or ideas for future podcasts, you can email us at speakingofpsychology at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 如果您对未来的播客有任何意见或想法，可以给我们发送电子邮件，邮箱是 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology is produced by Lee Weinerman.
sentences.zh: 《心理学话你知》由李·韦纳曼 (Lee Weinerman) 制作。

sentences.en: Our sound editor is Chris Kondayan.
sentences.zh: 我们的音响剪辑师是克里斯·孔达扬 (Chris Kondayan)。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢您的收听。

sentences.en: For the American Psychological Association, I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是美国心理学协会的金·米尔斯 (Kim Mills)。
